title: Custom Supply Chain Flow Visualization
business: Logistics managers tracking global inventory transit.
problem: Standard charting tools fail to represent complex, non-linear supply chain nodes and multi-path dependencies, leading to opaque inventory visibility.
solution: D3.js provides a low-level toolbox to map custom data structures directly to SVG elements, allowing for bespoke path-based visualizations that reflect actual transit routes.
steps: Parse raw transit data using d3-dsv.
Define d3-scale linear and band scales to map geographical coordinates to SVG space.
Utilize d3-selection to bind data to SVG path elements.
Apply d3-shape to generate curved lines representing transit routes.
Implement d3-zoom to allow users to navigate complex network clusters.
outcome: Improved clarity in identifying transit bottlenecks through custom-rendered network paths.
limitation: D3 is not a monolithic charting library; it requires manual composition of primitives, which increases development time. Check complexity by auditing the number of discrete modules required for a single view.

questions.question: In Custom Supply Chain Flow Visualization, what is a primary trade-off when using D3?
options: It is too simple and lacks advanced geometric capabilities.
It requires manual composition of primitives, increasing development time.
It cannot handle large datasets due to performance constraints.
It forces users to adopt a specific chart type for every visualization.
questions.explanation: D3 is not a monolithic library, meaning developers must manually assemble parts, which is a known trade-off for its flexibility.
